sapience_notes.subject: Sapience daily 2000-object extraction cap is not enforced as a hard stop
sapience_notes.value: On this machine (anthropic backend, claude-haiku-4-5), a single ordinary 50-chunk sapience-sync pass staged 2010 objects and the coverage line reported 'sapience yield: 2051 objects today (cap 2000)' -- the run completed all 50 chunks and was not truncated, dropped, or stopped early despite exceeding the stated daily cap within one run. The cap line appears to be cumulative/informational bookkeeping only, not an enforced ceiling that interrupts an in-progress or subsequent run.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience per-pass knowledge-object yield varies widely for an identical 50-chunk run
sapience_notes.value: Three fully-measured sapience-sync passes on the same machine, each attempting exactly 50 chunks (MAX_CHUNKS default), yielded 1208, 550, and 2010 staged objects respectively (24.16, 10.78, and 40.2 objects/chunk) -- a ~3.7x spread driven by the actual content of whichever 50 chunks were selected that day, not by a fixed per-chunk rate. Any extraction-cadence decision based on a single pass's yield is unreliable; a short series is needed to see the range.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience non-overridable subagent/harness-started filter ratio is stable over time
sapience_notes.value: Across 5 independent sapience coverage readings taken over 5 days on this machine, the ratio of 'skipped (subagent / harness-started transcripts)' to 'skipped (headless/agent)' held in a narrow 30.13x-31.45x band even as both counters grew by roughly 53-54% in absolute terms. The non-overridable filter consistently removes about 30x more transcripts than the overridable one, and this asymmetry is not a one-reading artifact.

sapience_notes.subject: systemctl --user start sapience-sync.service exceeds the Bash tool's default foreground timeout
sapience_notes.value: sapience-sync passes observed on this machine run 22-48 minutes wall clock, well past the harness's 120-second default foreground Bash timeout. Issuing `systemctl --user start sapience-sync.service` as a plain foreground call causes the harness to auto-background it; the correct follow-up is bounded foreground polling of `systemctl --user show -p ActiveState --value sapience-sync.service` in ~580-second chunks (looping while the value is 'activating' or 'active', since this Type=oneshot unit never transitions through a bare 'active' state visible to --quiet checks) rather than arming a Monitor or run_in_background wait on the poll itself.
